boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: 项目概况受限富文本 patch handler（G7.4，ADR-006 批准后首切片）。 数据契约：contracts/domain/overview-rich-text-patch.yaml v1。 单阶段协议（与 G7.2 同型——单记录单字段常规写）： - project.overview.rich_text.patch：kill switch gate（默认关，fail-closed）→ 参数/长度校验（claim 之前，纯输入错误不占幂等行）→ nh3 sanitize-on-save（净化失败 fail-closed 不落库）→ claim/complete 幂等 （G7-INFRA 定式，指纹绑定客户端摘要基线 + 新内容摘要——响应丢失后 的原样重试命中 replay 分支）→ expected 摘要基线比对（仅对首次执行 生效，与重放通道互不冲突）→ savepoint 内 write(overview_html) → sc.audit.log before/after（摘要 + 长度，不落全文）。 安全边界（ADR-006 决策 7 / G7.1 kill switch 模式）： - 专用组 group_sc_cap_rich_text_editor（不并入既有业务组）； - kill switch ir.config_parameter sc.rich_text_editor.enabled 默认关闭 （noupdate 数据文件，运维显式开启；关闭时结构化 CAPABILITY_DISABLED）； - intent 中间件对 is_write() 先组检查后 flag gate（无组+开关关 → PERMISSION_DENIED 而非 CAPABILITY_DISABLED，与 G7.1 同口径）； - 回退面 = kill switch + ACL + intent 不注册即不可达 + 净化 fail-closed。

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Company ownership of the P1 price libraries. ``sc.labor.price``, ``sc.equipment.price`` and ``sc.subcontract.price`` carry commercial price facts. Before this slice they declared no company at all and their record rules scoped project membership only, so a price row of another company stayed readable and writable for any internal user. The company is not a second, independently editable fact: it is derived from the owning project (``related="project_id.company_id", store=True``), exactly like the sibling ``sc.material.price`` derives it from its catalogue. That removes the duplicate declaration and the tautological project/company constraint. These checks read model source and the record-rule XML, so the boundary stays provable in the dependency-free inner loop without an Odoo server.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Navigation authorization reads ACL-visible menu carriers, not renderables. Regression pin for a declared product carrier that carries no action (a scene-entry page such as the role home). Odoo's ``_visible_menu_ids`` is action-centric: it can only ever return menus that carry a resolvable action, or that are ancestors of one. Using that renderable set as the *authorization* authority made one declared menu unobservable and silently dropped it from the delivered navigation even though the request user's groups allow the menu node. The two questions are separate: * rendering -> "which action menus would Odoo show" (``export_visible_menu_facts``) * authorization -> "do this user's groups allow this carrier" (``export_authorized_menu_facts``)

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Behavioural lock: the list page-size declarations are consumed through the real runtime carrier, not through a guessed key path. Defect this covers (found on the daily server right after PR #621 was deployed): `resolveActionViewPageSizeOptions/Range` read `searchContract.defaults` straight off whatever object they were handed, while `ActionView.vue` hands them the normalised contract store. That store exposes the snapshot under `.snapshot` only, so the lookup always produced `{}` even though the backend declared `page_size_options = [10, 20, 50]`; the list surface then stopped with `ContractGapError search.defaults.page_size_options` and declared no presentation surface at all. The assertions drive the production helpers with the production store factory, so a regression cannot pass by matching declaration strings alone. The negative case is asserted from a working baseline first: the same helper resolves the declaration, then stops only once the declaration is actually removed.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Row activation identity must come from the contract's row placement. The backend `normalize_target_scope` collapses native placement (header / toolbar / smart / row) into the closed V2 target-scope vocabulary, so header actions also carry `targetScope: 'page'`. A row-activation lookup that accepts `targetScope === 'page'` therefore matches the first header action and can navigate a row click to a header action's target. These cases bind the navigation runtime to the declared row placement instead.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Executable proof for the collaboration region authority. The collaboration region renders when, and only when, the contract declares it and the dispatch context does not suppress it. The declaration read is stated once, in `contractRuntimeVm.ts`; this test executes the real module so the rule cannot be retired by rearranging tokens: a read that cannot refuse a contract that declares no region, or that accepts a surface of any content kind, changes at least one expectation below. The tables run twice: once under node, and once with browser globals installed. A rule that is live under node and inert in the browser is a different rule, and the second pass is what makes that visible here instead of in the product.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Behavioural lock for the single frontend contract-stop primitive. The primitive's job is to make a missing or invalid declaration stop the surface instead of letting the frontend repair it. These cases drive the production helpers, so a regression that re-introduces coercion cannot pass by matching a declaration string: `true` must not become `1`, `'20'` must not become `20`, `1.9` must not be truncated to `1`, and a legal declaration must be returned unchanged.

Why this exists --------------- The repository drives two very different audiences from one ``make`` surface: the remote required gates (``public_guard`` / ``merge_policy_gate`` / ``professional_quality_gate`` / ``frontend_release_gate``) and the governed local lane (``ci.local.quick``). Both are hand-maintained target lists, so they drift. A guard executed only by ``ci.local.quick`` merges green remotely and only fails at the local exact-head Quick; a guard executed only remotely makes a local pass prove something different from a remote pass. That divergence is the structural reason a remote result cannot be reused locally, and it is the reason "CI green / local red" keeps recurring. This instrument measures that divergence instead of arguing about it: * make target inventory plus its prerequisite / ``$(MAKE)`` recursion graph; * which targets each declared gate anchor can reach; * which guard scripts each execution lane actually executes; * which targets and scripts are referenced nowhere at all (dead surface). ``--check`` compares the measurement with ``verification_lane_baseline.json``. boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Enforce the contract structure lock. Regenerates the contract structure fingerprint from the current code and compares it against the committed baseline in ``contracts/generated/contract_structure_fingerprint.json``. boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Parse first-party Node sources without executing them. Peer of ``python_syntax_check.py`` for the ``.mjs``/``.cjs``/``.js`` delivery corpus. Frontend acceptance runners, Node verify scripts and the Odoo browser assets under ``addons/**/static/src`` are only executed by the surface-specific make target (or the browser) that owns them, so a file that breaks syntactically can land through any other change with no gate observing it. This checker keeps one cheap corpus-wide gate: every tracked first-party Node file must parse. ``.mjs`` and ``.cjs`` declare their module format, so ``node --check <file>`` parses them directly. ``.js`` does not: the runtime resolves it to CommonJS, or retries it as an ES module when the CommonJS parse fails on ES-module syntax. ``node --check <file>.js`` returns 0 *without parsing the file at all* whenever that resolution picks the ES module (measured on node 22.17.0 and 24.16.0), so trusting it would leave a detected module's syntax errors unobserved. Every ``.js`` file is therefore parsed from stdin with an explicit ``--input-type``: CommonJS first, then the ES module. A file passes when either format parses, which is the set the runtime itself accepts.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Bounded, deterministic parallelism shared by the governed scan members. One mechanism, three call sites. The secrets, personal-data and clean-history passes all enumerate Git blobs and then run pure per-blob rules with no cross-blob state. A missing or mismatched file is refused, never written. Read-only unless ``--apply`` is passed with ``--archive-root``.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Retire an unbound structural form config that a bound native surface owns. A published ``view_orchestration:<model>:form:action:<id>:view:0`` contract is a low-code edit saved without a resolved view target. When a view-bound native semantic surface owns the same (model, action, form) scope, the runtime view orchestrator must fail closed (``CONFIG_TARGET_BINDING_REQUIRED``) rather than let a second structural declaration compete with the authoritative native surface; the whole page then returns 400. When the edit is stale — every field it declares already reaches the page from the scope's native arch and field policy — retiring the config is the truthful repair instead of inventing a patch body for it. Deliberately narrow: it only touches the exact contract id named by ``SC_REPAIR_CONTRACT_ID``, and only when that record still matches the unbound structural low-code form identity for a scope that also carries a view-bound native semantic surface. Dry-run by default; ``APPLY=1`` performs the retirement and prints the authoritative readback.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Behavioural test for the unbound structural form-config repair driver. The driver is a stdin script executed inside ``odoo shell`` (``bash scripts/ops/odoo_shell_exec.sh < scripts/ops/repair_unbound_structural_form_contract.py``), so it cannot be imported: its body runs against the ambient ``env``. The behaviour that matters is therefore exercised by executing the *same source* in a sandbox with a stub ``env``, which drives the real decision tree the database run used instead of asserting on text. What is locked here is the fail-closed ladder, because every rung guards a write against a live demo database: * an unresolved target, an unpublished config, a view-bound config, a config that declares no structural form, or a name that is not the unbound low-code form identity all stop *before* the write; * a scope with no view-bound native semantic surface refuses to retire anything (``SC_REPAIR_CONTRACT_ID`` on the wrong scope must not delete a real config); * without ``APPLY=1`` the run is a dry run that publishes the verdict and performs no write and no commit; * with ``APPLY=1`` the only mutation is ``active=False`` on the exact target, followed by a commit and an authoritative read

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Bind the acceptance surface to every code change. A change is only "covered" when the paths it touches are declared in the acceptance evolution registry and the acceptance suites that registry requires are either: * executed by the same governed lane (contract/governance suites), or * backed by an exact-head evidence manifest produced by a real runtime run. The plan half is deterministic and runs in every PR/local lane. The evidence half is fail-closed and is required by ``make pr.merge``. HEAD is provenance, not an invalidation key: a suite may reuse evidence from an ancestor only while its declared input fingerprint and evidence bytes are identical. Any changed suite layer still has to be executed at the evaluated head. Exit codes: 0 pass, 1 binding/evidence failure, 2 usage or registry error.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Fail closed on any field declared by more than one class block. One field fact has exactly one declaration site. A second class that re-declares the same field does not override the first: Odoo merges both definitions attribute by attribute, so the effective field is a union that neither file shows. Adding ``help``, ``string``, ``index`` or ``readonly`` in another class therefore silently changes the first declaration instead of extending it. This guard is intentionally stricter than the money-fact registry: there is no registration escape hatch for a duplicate. Consolidate the attributes into the owning declaration, or create a new field with a distinct name.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Canonical scanner for backend model field declarations. Odoo merges same-name field definitions from every class block on a model attribute by attribute. Two declarations are therefore one hidden union, not an override: the surviving field is the union of both classes and neither file alone shows the effective definition. This module is the single scanner behind the strict declaration guard and the money-fact declaration guard, so both lanes use one definition of "duplicate". The scanner is static. It never imports Odoo and never touches a database.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Falsifiable, container-free assertions for the collection-capability rule. The list surface publishes one declared action list; ``import`` may only appear there when the caller's *effective rights* allow ``create`` on a model that has a list view and at least one importable field. A README cannot prove that, and a runtime census only samples the models that happen to be reachable, so the rule is locked here against the pure function that implements it. What is asserted is the mechanism, not the presence of a string: * ``import`` is declared exactly when ``rights.create`` is true (a biconditional sweep, so a future "just add import for this model" cannot pass); * absence of rights never promotes a capability (fail-closed, not inferred); * the declaration is a pure function of (selection_actions, rights, fields_map, has_list_view) — it has no model/surface/action parameter, so a per-model special case is not expressible; * ``batch_policy`` is the ``selection`` projection of that same declaration, so an empty declaration yields an empty policy instead of a second derivation.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Single authority for the frontend decision-authority ledger. Why this module exists ---------------------- The product goal is: "a customised frontend derives everything except rendering and interaction from the runtime contract." That sentence only becomes decidable when it is turned into a finite, reviewable check: * every decision-shaped expression inside the frontend decision scopes (``pages`` / ``views`` / ``app``) is detected by a named rule; * every detection is either declared render/interaction, registered in this ledger with an explicit classification and an evidence pointer, or a failure; * ``contract-derived`` intent literals are verified against the *published* contract export (``docs/contract/exports/intent_catalog.json``) instead of a frozen string list, so the check stays structural rather than literal; * ``contract-projectable-gap`` entries are the actionable backlog -- frontend decisions that have no contract carrier yet but can be projected by the backend. They are the only legitimate remaining distance to the goal; * ``frontend-logic-defect`` entries are frontend business logic that contradicts or bypasses the contract. The ledger is regenerated from this module

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Mobile viewport contract guard (G4 incremental closure). R-G4-01: the SPA declares `env(safe-area-inset-*)` paddings in shell and form pages. Without `viewport-fit=cover` in the viewport meta those environment variables are always 0 on notched devices, silently disabling the safe-area handling. This guard fail-closes on: 1. index.html viewport meta missing `width=device-width`, `initial-scale=1` or `viewport-fit=cover`. 2. Any style using `env(safe-area-inset-` while viewport-fit=cover is absent (cross-file consistency). 3. `user-scalable=no` / `maximum-scale=1` regressions (accessibility floor: zoom must not be disabled).

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Fail when a list-surface claim is bound to evidence that does not support it. The page-pattern ledgers bind a conclusion to a concrete observation, e.g. ``... gates 108/108 list-surface checks ...``. This was a real defect: ``collection.header-actions`` and ``collection.toolbar-surface`` cited ``.runtime/final-acceptance/list-surface-structure.json`` as ``316/316 gated``, but that mutable path had since been overwritten by a payment.request create/edit run whose document records ``records 12/12`` and ``gated 0/0``. The ledger therefore asserted list-surface coverage that no artifact supported — and the guard itself depended on a machine-local file that may not exist at all on another checkout. A ``source_bounded`` entry is deliberately *not* rendered: that model already carries the named global ir.rule the declaration points at, and emitting a second ceiling would duplicate one fact. The coverage guard verifies the named rule, so the declaration stays the single source for both paths. ``--check`` regenerates in memory and fails when the committed file differs, so the generated output can never drift from the declaration.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Unit lock on the contract gate's declared per-case volatile response keys. The gate compares a regenerated snapshot against the tracked reference. A case whose response carries a value assigned by the producing environment (for example a database row handle) may declare that member name under ``volatile_keys``. The declaration is *per case* and must stay discriminating: it may only suppress the declared member, never anything else, and a malformed declaration must fail closed. These tests drive the real ``scripts/contract/gate_contract.sh`` with a stub export command, so they need no database and prove the declared semantics deterministically. The product-side assertions at the end pin the declaration to the single preference case and prove that the tracked reference no longer carries the environment-assigned handle.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Test coverage registry: bind declared Odoo test groups to a governed entry. Why this exists (2026-10-10 nightly triage): the repository declared a large number of Odoo test groups through ``@tagged(...)`` and shipped ``scripts/ci/test_*.py`` unit scripts, but nothing proved that a declared group was ever *executed* by a governed entry. The 2026-10-09 nightly proved the gap is not theoretical: * the ``Run backend test suite per module`` step aborted on its first failing module (errexit was never disabled), so every later module - and its group coverage - was silently skipped and still reported as a pass; * ``uc4_native_lowcode`` (16 test files) was "verified" once by hand and then had no recurring gate at all; * ``scripts/ci/test_backend_test_suite_dispatch_contract.py`` existed with zero make/workflow references. This tool makes the gap machine-checkable. It inventories every declared group and every ``scripts/ci/test_*.py`` unit script, resolves whether a governed test-selection entry reaches it, and fails closed when a group is neither gated nor explicitly dispositioned in ``scripts/verify/test_coverage_registry.yaml``. Reachability tiers (deliberately conservative): * ``gated``

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Prove the backend's own action-declaration side is complete. A transition the backend lets a user execute must carry a published business purpose, because the Web is not allowed to infer one from a method name, a label or a button position. This guard reads the declaration authorities (instead of a rendered page) and fails when any of them can hand the Web a reachable action whose meaning is missing or outside the published vocabulary. The registry is read by static evaluation, not by importing Odoo: a value is resolved when it is a literal, a small comprehension over a literal model list, or a call to another declaration helper in the same file. Anything else is reported instead of silently skipped. Whether an action is reachable is also decided by permission and role, so the same guard proves the authorization side: an action the backend offers must resolve a runtime authorization verdict and, when it declares a role gate, that gate must name a role from the published role vocabulary and a group the module actually declares. A dangling or invented gate is a failure, not a warning. This proves the *declaration* side only. A native view may still contain buttons no authority regist

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Single static reader for the workflow contract profile registry. ``workflow_contract_service.PROFILE_BY_MODEL`` mixes inline literals with helper-generated entries:: PROFILE_BY_MODEL = { "payment.request": {...}, **_simple_approval_profiles(("sc.equipment.plan", ...)), } A regex over the source text only sees the inline half. A consumer that trusted such a pattern silently scanned a subset of the contract -- the failure mode that hid seven native buttons on the 25 helper-built models. This module evaluates the dict expression instead, so every profile is present however it was written. Only literal expressions are supported: an unsupported node raises :class:`ProfileSourceError` rather than returning a partial mapping, because a consumer must never silently scan a subset of the contract.

boundary_answers.what_it_verifies: Every raw workflow state a profile can meet is mapped to a business phase. ``WorkflowContractService.describe_record`` derives the published phase with:: business_phase = profile["state_phase"].get(raw_state, raw_state or "unknown") so a raw state the profile does not map is not an error: it silently becomes the raw token and is then handed to ``_editability``, ``_approval_phase`` and the statusbar projection. A model whose ``Selection`` grew a value therefore keeps looking healthy while a real business phase falls through the fallback path -- the same "silent subset" failure this family already hit once, when a regex read only the inline half of the profile registry. The guard closes the set in both directions, statically from the addon sources: * **coverage** -- every value the profile's ``state_field`` Selection can take must be a key of ``state_phase``; a missing key is FAIL; * **dead entries** -- a ``state_phase`` or ``state_actions`` key the Selection can never produce is dead configuration. It is not deleted by the guard (that is a profile edit, not a guard decision) but it must be registered in ``config/contract/workflow_state_phase_dead_entries.v1.json`` with a reason, so
